prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of one outdoor area of a high starlit plateau of grass, heather and grey rock in a fantasy JRPG world as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted colour ramps, dark warm outlines, lush natural detail), classic top-down RPG map view seen from above with a slight 3/4 tilt (tree crowns, rocks and buildings seen from above with their south-facing sides visible; NOT an isometric view, NOT a diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render, no perspective).

THE PLACE: A GREAT METEOR CRATER ON A HIGH PLATEAU: cool silver-green grass and heather around it; in the middle a deep round crater bowl ringed by a rim of broken grey rock, its inner floor flat dark slate rock with clusters of faceted pale-blue CRYSTALS growing from it and a small ruined stone altar at the very bottom; a footpath leads from the west down a ramp into the crater; the pale road runs from the west edge round the north of the crater to the north edge; grey rock cliffs along the south and east edges; a few dark pines. Palette: silver greens, mauve heather, dark slate, glassy pale blue and white crystals, grey rock. Strange, hushed, glittering.

The crater rim is a continuous ring of rock (no gaps) except where the footpath ramp goes down on the west side. The CRYSTALS are small separate clusters exactly where the guide shows them.

The FIRST attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE drawn on a 52 x 40 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output; the output is 2496 x 1920 px). Trace over it: your painting is laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and used directly as the walkable game map, so every road, shore, cliff, wall, tree mass, water body and landmark must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size (keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide; do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep the exact width of the roads and of the one- and two-tile gaps).

The SECOND attached image is only a STYLE REFERENCE from the same game: match its pixel-art rendering (pixel size, clusters, outlines, hue-shifted ramps, level of detail), but use the palette of THE PLACE below. Do NOT copy anything from it (no buildings, piers, water or objects from it).

The guide is soft colour-coding only (its blurred edges only mean the edge is natural and free-flowing): do NOT copy its flat colours, straight tile steps, circles or stripes. Interpret every area as the real material with rich natural variation, and give shores, meadows, rocks and cliffs natural, organic, slightly irregular outlines (bulging or receding by at most a third of a tile around the guide edge). Make it feel like a real, exciting place to explore, full of small natural detail.

Guide colour key:
- green = short highland GRASS (walkable, flat): cool silver-green turf of a high plateau with tiny white and blue flowers.
- olive green with short purple strokes = low purple HEATHER and tufts of tall grass (walkable, low, flat).
- green with small blue/white dots = little blue STAR FLOWERS in the grass (walkable).
- light tan band = the ROAD: an old road of pale packed earth with sunken pale paving stones showing through and small stones along its edges (walkable).
- darker brown = a narrow FOOTPATH of trodden earth (walkable).
- light grey with block lines = pale FLAGSTONES / worn stone steps / paving (walkable, flat).
- dark slate grey with small arcs = FLAT DARK ROCK (walkable): the level floor of a crater, dark rock with a few pebbles, level with the ground around it.
- blue = a small POND (not walkable).
- dark green = dense PINE WOOD on the slopes below (not walkable): dark conifer crowns packed together.
- dark green circles = single PINES (not walkable): dark alpine pines seen from above.
- round green-olive blobs = small juniper BUSHES (not walkable).
- grey circles = BOULDERS (not walkable).
- all colour areas are LEVEL GROUND unless listed as not walkable; only the cliffs below are raised.
- grey with horizontal strata and a green top edge = grey ROCK CLIFFS (not walkable): sheer layered grey stone faces, grass overhanging the top edge, fallen rocks at their foot.
Landmarks (paint each exactly on its block, at the block's size):
- the blocks in colour rgb(140,200,250) = clusters of glowing pale BLUE CRYSTALS growing from the dark rock, sharp and faceted.
- the blocks in colour rgb(180,176,190) = a small RUINED ALTAR of pale stone at the crater bottom, cracked, a star carved on its top.
Walkable areas must stay walkable-looking: no boulders, trees, fences, crates or objects standing on them unless the guide shows them.

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps. Characters in this game are about 72 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer (the game darkens it into night at runtime and adds lamp light on top). Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light as in the style reference; NO darkness, NO night tint, NO long cast shadows, NO light pools, NO glow halo, NO vignette, NO fog over the map, NO clouds over the map.
Do NOT paint any characters, people, animals, monsters, birds, boats or ships on the water (unless a landmark says so), treasure chests, lanterns, lamp posts, torches, campfires, signs, signposts, text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, borders, frames or UI. Those are added later as separate sprites: leave the ground open for them.
revised_prompt: Generate ONE complete finished 2496x1920 top-down playable fantasy JRPG outdoor map, editing/tracing the user's FIRST supplied 52x40 tile layout guide faithfully as the spatial image reference, and using the SECOND supplied image ONLY as pixel-art style reference. Maintain landmark positions, relative scale, road/path widths, and all outlines very closely, without mirroring or moving. Premium detailed crisp hand-placed square-pixel art, subtle 3/4 top down RPG view (not isometric). Great meteor crater on high silver-green grass and mauve-heather plateau. Road enters from west at y~900, winds northeast past northwest of crater, bends north to top edge at x~1240. Thin brown footpath comes from west at y~1200 to x~930 and runs down west rim ramp into crater. Crater centered ~1390,1260, approx outer diameter 1150x780, with CONTINUOUS broken grey rock rim except western path ramp; slate-dark flat floor with SMALL precisely placed separate glowing pale-blue faceted crystal clusters following blue guide blocks (two at northern floor, one northeast, one west, one southwest, two south-central, one southeastern) and small cracked pale-star-carved ruined stone altar at guide's single lilac block near center x1390 y1220. Keep all separate crystals small. South and eastern edges are layered grey cliffs, top edge grass overhang, fallen stone; cliff stretches x2200-2496 on east, full southern edge y~1790-1920. Three groups of dark pine crowns at northwest x250-550 y320-480, northeast x1770-1930 y220-380, southwest x380-620 y1470-1630, plus mapped single juniper shrubs and small boulders at guide positions. Sprinkles of tiny white/blue flowers in marked meadows; bright neutral daylight albedo, hushed starlit thematic objects but NO night lighting, darkness, halo or bloom. Organic slight pixelated irregularity in natural edges within 1/3 tile of guide. Hue-shifted color ramps, warm dark outlines, rich carefully controlled pixel clusters, detailed cliffs and foliage matching second reference's pixel scale. No text, UI, grid, frame, people, animal, added props, fog, painterly strokes, blur, antialiasing, diorama or 3D.
